gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Apple's base M4 and M5 MacBook Air drive two external displays alongside the built-in screen, so a two-screen extender can run both panels without a driver on them. On a base M3 Air the second external display works only with the lid closed, which an extender clipped to the lid cannot do.
standout_why: I opened deskgearhq.com's guide (2026-07-26). It never names an Apple chip or says how many displays a Mac can drive. It also says every pick, including the Trio 3 Pro, runs both screens 'over a single USB-C cable using DisplayPort Alt Mode' with no driver, but Macworld says the Trio 3 Pro uses two USB-C cables and needs software on base M1/M2 Macs. ChatGPT's own answer said only that base M1/M2/M3 Macs are 'generally limited to one' and left out the M4/M5 Air. I could not open the cited rival pages (FOPO S11 and tutt.ca returned HTTP 429, Plugable returned 429, Best Buy timed out) or gradedpicks.com (certificate error). So I can't rule out that one of them has part of this, and I scored 2 rather than 3.
decides: For the many shoppers on a MacBook Air, this settles which kind of screen to buy. A base M4 or M5 Air can run a two-screen extender (FOPO S7 or S11, or the Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro on its two cables) with no driver. A base M1, M2 or M3 Air with the lid open gets only one driver-free added screen. For those owners the honest driver-free pick is a single-screen extender like the Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS, or a two-screen unit plus the maker's software, which means it is no longer driver-free. Windows laptops still need one video-capable USB-C port per added screen.

findings.label: MacBook Air (13-inch, M4, 2025): external displays alongside the built-in screen
findings.value: Up to two external displays, up to 6K at 60 Hz, while the built-in display stays at full native resolution; native DisplayPort 1.4 output over USB-C
findings.note: Display Support section. Apple writes 'Simultaneously supports full native resolution on the built-in display ... and: Up to two external displays', so both work with the lid open.

findings.label: MacBook Air (M5): external displays alongside the built-in screen
findings.value: Up to two external displays (two at up to 6K 60 Hz, or one at up to 8K 60 Hz); built-in display supported at full native resolution at the same time
findings.source_title: MacBook Air 13- and 15-inch with M5 - Tech Specs - Apple
findings.note: Same for the 13- and 15-inch models. Apple also says 'up to two external displays over a single Thunderbolt port'. It doesn't say whether a non-Thunderbolt extender on one USB-C cable can use that, so we don't claim it.

findings.label: MacBook Air (13-inch, M3, 2024): second external display
findings.value: One external display (up to 6K 60 Hz) with the built-in screen on; a second external display (up to 5K 60 Hz) only with the lid closed
findings.note: Apple's wording: 'Close the MacBook Air lid to use a second external display'. A screen extender mounts on the open lid, so a base M3 Air gets one driver-free added screen. That conclusion is our inference from Apple's spec.

findings.label: Which MacBooks run both screens without software
findings.value: Any M1/M2/M3 Pro or Max, or any M4/M5 MacBook, needs no software. Base M1, base M2 and the MacBook Neo need Mobile Pixels' free software. Both screens connect with the two included USB-C cables
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review (Macworld, Simon Jary, Apr 2, 2026)
findings.note: Simon Jary (Macworld) wrote that plain (non-Pro/Max) M1 and M2 Macs plus the new MacBook Neo are limited to connecting just a single monitor, so their users must download and install free software. He also wrote that 'The screens connect to the MacBook with the included two USB-C cables.' This contradicts deskgearhq's single-cable, no-driver claim.

findings.label: Maker's condition for driver-free use
findings.value: Driver-free only from a USB-C port with DisplayPort; otherwise 'additional drivers will be needed'
findings.note: The FAQ says: 'If your computer has a USB-C port with DisplayPort enabled (this is built into the computer)... Otherwise additional drivers will be needed to use the Trio.' It also says a USB-A port on Catalina needs the driver download.

findings.label: Rival guide's claim about Trio 3 Pro connection (for contrast)
findings.value: deskgearhq says all five picks, including the Trio 3 Pro, connect 'over a single USB-C cable using DisplayPort Alt Mode' with no driver on current macOS and Windows, and gives no chip or display-count limits
findings.note: This is a rival page from ChatGPT's results, recorded here to show what it gets wrong. It isn't a source for any spec. It credits its driver claims to Amazon listings and says independent lab testing of these products is limited.
